Retelling: On the journey around Edom, Israel grew impatient, spoke against God and Moses, and despised the manna, calling it worthless food. God sent fiery serpents among them, and many died from their bites. The people confessed they had sinned and begged Moses to pray, and Moses interceded. God did not remove the serpents; instead he told Moses to make a bronze serpent and set it on a pole, so that anyone bitten who looked at it would live. Moses did so, and every bitten person who looked in faith lived. Centuries later Jesus pointed to this lifted serpent as a picture of his own lifting up, so that whoever believes in him would not perish.
Discussion: The cure required looking, not earning: bitten people lived by trusting God's appointed means, and Jesus uses the same image for himself. Reflect: 1) Why is simply looking to God's provision hard when you feel the bite of sin? 2) How does this story shape your understanding of faith? 3) What does Moses' intercession teach you about praying for others?
Significance: God gave life through a look of faith at a lifted serpent, and Jesus himself made it a picture of salvation through his death, so the wilderness cure points directly to the cross.
